title.narrative: Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
To strengthen the capacity of employers’ organisations in implementing Convention. No. 190, the organization of employers of North Macedonia developed a new risk assessment tool which takes into account violence and harassment and its related psychosocial risks, including hazards and risks arise from discrimination. The tool, once validated, has been uploaded in the employers’ organisation website online tools and it is not available to all members. The main tool targets larger and medium-sized enterprises (employers, managers, workers representatives and workers) and OSH professionals. Additionally, a shorter version was adapted for use in micro and small enterprises. These tools seek to address, prevent, and mitigate violence and harassment in the world of work as part of occupational safety and health management at the enterprise level.
To increase awareness raising about Convention No. 190 and sensitize the public, in 2022 the Economic and Social Council, Trade Unions (SSM, KSS, UNASM), Employers organisations (ORM, BCM), the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection and the State Labour Inspectorate joined the ILO global campaign for workplaces free of violence and harassment, ratify C. 190. The ILO provided technical assistance for the elaboration of the Analysis of the alignment of the Macedonian legislation with the ILO Convention 190. This analysis was validated in a tripartite meeting organized by the ILO on 14 April 2022. In 2022, the ILO produced the video to promote the ratification of the ILO Convention 190. In 2022 the ILO promoted the Macedonian version of the ILO Guide on C190: E-Nasilstvo-i-voznemiruvanje-vo-rabotniot-svet-e-file-1.pdf (socijalendijalog.mk) In 2023 the ILO translated and adapted the Violence and harassment at work: A practical guide for employers. Between November and December 2022, the ILO conducted a desk review of existing risk assessment tools and assisted in the development of the draft tools. On 24 January 2023, the ILO organised a tripartite validation workshop to better understand the needs of all sizes of enterprises and collect the main issues raised by the workers' organizations. Additionally, the ILO hold a working meeting with Occupational Safety and Health experts to discuss potential approaches to be used in the assessment tools. Between August and September 2023 the ILO supported the validation of the tools, and in October 2023 it also provided support for the organisation of the workshop to present the tools and train enterprises' representatives on their use. In December 2023 , ILO supported the creation of the online website dedicated to violence and harassment at work that includes the risk assessment tools and the employers practical guide.
